meta.purpose: Data contract for the 5392 self-directed learner Practice Mode (Threshold Trainer + Troubleshooter). Consumed by ?role=practice. Field names match the engine / PACE scenario schema.

feedbackModes.training: Inline coaching — live nudges during the run + end debrief; unlimited hints.
feedbackModes.validation: Self-assessment — silent during the run; scorecard + best-practice debrief at end; only a validation pass counts toward skill sign-off.

meta.notes: Practice mode only sets existing scenario fields (rhythm,aRate,vRate,aThr,vThr,aSig,vSig,leadA,leadV,oversA,oversV,batt,connectionFault). Output & sensitivity are learner-operated device knobs, never scenario data.

captureThresholdMa.teaches: bad wire — recognize, do not just crank output

tolerances.note: Identification is judged against the hidden ground-truth value the engine used.

stimulationOutputMultiplier.source: LOCAL TRAINING STANDARD: set output to 2x threshold (DOUBLE, not triple). Rationale: a tighter margin unmasks a rising threshold / lead dislodgement sooner and preserves battery. Manufacturer allows 2-3x; we train to double. Coach a learner who cranks to 3x+ toward doubling instead.

sensitivityMaxFraction.source: Medtronic 5392: set sensitivity to 1/2 (or less) of the sensing threshold. Lower mV = more sensitive.

scenarioFrames.frame: POD 2, V-paced. Verify the ventricular capture threshold and set a safe output before the team rounds.
Threshold looked higher on the last check — reconfirm ventricular capture and set your margin.
Dual-chamber setup — confirm the atrial capture threshold and set a safe output.
The patient has their own rhythm — confirm the generator senses the ventricle before you leave it on demand.
Small-looking R waves on the strip — find the ventricular sensing threshold and set a safe sensitivity.
Confirm atrial sensing so tracking behaves before you hand off.

loss_of_capture.label: Loss of capture
loss_of_capture.recognitionCorrect: Loss of capture (pacing spikes present, no capture)
correctActions: Increase output to 2x the capture threshold (double, local training standard)
Ensure backup if the patient is dependent
loss_of_capture.deviceDetect: capture restored when output >= vThr/aThr (spike now followed by a paced complex)
safety: Confirm the patient is not stranded without capture while troubleshooting
loss_of_capture.escalateWhen: output at device maximum still without capture, or the threshold is >10 mA / climbing fast -> notify provider and plan alternative pacing (see escalationGuidance)
loss_of_capture.teaching: Spikes ARE present — the impulse fires but doesn't capture. Doubling output (or finding a rising threshold) fixes it; contrast with fracture where spikes vanish. If maxed output won't capture, stop cranking and escalate.

lead_fracture.label: Lead fracture
lead_fracture.recognitionCorrect: Lead fracture / broken wire (no pacing spikes)
correctActions: Recognize it is not learner-fixable at the bedside
Escalate for wire replacement
Bridge with transcutaneous pacing if dependent
lead_fracture.deviceDetect: no output path exists; raising output / going async does NOT restore capture
safety: Do not waste time cranking output; get a transcutaneous bridge for a dependent patient
lead_fracture.teaching: No spikes = output isn't reaching the heart. A fracture is inside the wire — unlike a cable disconnect, the learner can't reconnect it.

cable_disconnect.label: Disconnected cable at generator
cable_disconnect.recognitionCorrect: Cable disconnected at the generator (open circuit, no spikes)
correctActions: Work the circuit generator->cable->terminal->wire
Reconnect the cable at the generator port (verify click + gentle tug)
cable_disconnect.deviceDetect: connectionFault cleared -> circuit closed -> output/spikes resume
safety: Transcutaneous bridge for a dependent patient while you find the open point
cable_disconnect.teaching: Looks like a fracture (no spikes) but is FIXABLE — the learner reconnects at the generator. This is why cable-disconnect and fracture are distinct mechanics.

undersensing.label: Undersensing / competition
undersensing.recognitionCorrect: Undersensing — competitive pacing (spikes marching into intrinsic beats)
correctActions: Increase sensitivity (LOWER the mV number) toward ~1/2 the R-wave
Confirm the generator now inhibits on intrinsic beats
undersensing.deviceDetect: sensitivity setting <= signal amplitude -> intrinsic beats sensed -> competition stops
safety: Competition risks R-on-T -> VT/VF; correct promptly
undersensing.escalateWhen: sensitivity at its most-sensitive limit (mV floor) and the device still won't sense the intrinsic signal -> notify provider; the signal may be too small (wire issue) and need repositioning/alternative pacing
undersensing.teaching: Device fails to see the patient's beats and paces on top. Lower mV = more sensitive. Opposite fix to oversensing. If you reach the sensitivity limit and it still can't sense, escalate.

oversensing.label: Oversensing
oversensing.recognitionCorrect: Oversensing — inappropriate inhibition (pauses, no spikes when needed)
correctActions: Decrease sensitivity (RAISE the mV number) or pace asynchronously
Treat the noise source (shivering, loose connections)
oversensing.deviceDetect: noise no longer inhibits (sensitivity raised) OR async mode -> consistent pacing resumes
safety: In a dependent patient, oversensing pauses are life-threatening — rescue first (async), fine-tune after
oversensing.escalateWhen: sensitivity at its least-sensitive limit and/or async still not delivering reliable pacing, or the noise source can't be removed -> notify provider and plan alternative pacing
oversensing.teaching: Device is fooled by noise and inhibits when the patient needs pacing. No spikes, like a fracture — but the patient is dependent and the strip shows inhibition, not open circuit. If limits are reached without a stable rescue, escalate.

dependence_no_pacing.label: Needs pacing now
correctActions: Recognize instability
Call for help / escalate
Initiate pacing per order or bridge transcutaneously
dependence_no_pacing.deviceDetect: pacing initiated with capture -> adequate paced rate restored
safety: Transcutaneous bridge + ACLS bradycardia pathway if unstable
dependence_no_pacing.teaching: The fault is the patient, not the device. Recognize the need, escalate, and (within scope) initiate pacing.

battery.label: Battery failing
correctActions: Recognize the battery alarm/indicator
Replace battery/generator without interrupting a dependent patient
battery.deviceDetect: battery restored -> pacing maintained without a gap
safety: Have a replacement ready before interrupting pacing in a dependent patient
battery.teaching: Plan the swap so a dependent patient never loses pacing.

aflutter_rap.label: Atrial flutter — overdrive pacing
correctActions: Confirm flutter (not AF)
Confirm order + defibrillator on the patient
Deliver RAP 20-30 ppm above the atrial rate for a brief hold
aflutter_rap.deviceDetect: RAP delivered via atrial wires; observe conversion to sinus vs proarrhythmia
safety: RAP will not convert AF; defibrillator immediately available; watch for AF/VF induction
aflutter_rap.teaching: Advanced, physician-directed. Recognition + safe setup matter as much as the delivery.

underlying_rhythm_check.label: Assess underlying rhythm (dependent patient)
underlying_rhythm_check.recognitionCorrect: Pacemaker-dependent — assess underlying rhythm SAFELY (do not unplug cables)
recognitionDistractors: Safe to unplug the bridging cables to check
No need to reassess — leave it paced
Increase output to test underlying rhythm
correctActions: Gradually step the paced RATE down (or use a brief PAUSE) while watching the monitor
Keep continuous ECG + arterial monitoring and transcutaneous pacing/defib ready
Restore pacing promptly if no underlying rhythm returns; NEVER unplug the bridging cables
underlying_rhythm_check.deviceDetect: paced rate reduced gradually OR Pause used (NOT a cable disconnect); pacing restored after the check
safety: Dependent/asystole patient: unplugging cables removes instant restore capability — never do it; backup pacing ready; restore immediately if asystole persists
underlying_rhythm_check.escalateWhen: n/a (this is a safe assessment maneuver, not a fault) — but if underlying asystole persists, confirm continued dependence and keep backup pacing immediately available
underlying_rhythm_check.teaching: The safe way to look for a returning underlying rhythm in a dependent patient is to step the rate down gradually or use Pause under full monitoring — NOT to unplug the bridging cables, which strands a dependent patient. Post-op asystole = plan to stay paced.

escalationGuidance.purpose: Surface as an inline coach rec (training) and in the debrief whenever the learner has exhausted device + wire troubleshooting. Reinforces knowing WHEN to stop adjusting and get help.
triggers: Output at the device maximum without consistent capture
Capture threshold in/above the reposition-replace band (>10 mA) or climbing fast across checks
Sensitivity adjusted to its limit and the sensing problem persists (still under- or over-sensing)
Repeated loss of capture despite doubling output and completing connection/circuit checks
Oversensing that cannot be rescued or whose noise source cannot be removed
recommendedActions: Notify the provider / EP that device and wire troubleshooting is exhausted
Plan for alternative pacing: transcutaneous pacing NOW as a bridge; anticipate transvenous pacing or new epicardial wires
Keep transcutaneous pacing + a defibrillator ready; do not leave a dependent patient
escalationGuidance.note: This is the 'don't keep cranking' lesson: at max output / sensitivity limits with an unresolved capture or sensing problem, escalation + an alternative-pacing plan is the correct next step, not further device adjustment.

troubleshooter.curatedNote: Draw the 11 PACE cases in random order; re-randomize their hidden thresholds within band each run so a familiar case still plays differently.

rules: Spawn only fault x rhythm pairs listed in validityMatrix; drop (and log) anything else.
Set dependence via vRate 0 (chb/asystole) so failed pacing = no escape.
For aflutter, omit aRate (inherent ~300 exceeds the 0-180 slider) and set vRate ~150 for 2:1 — same rule as PACE-9.
Express cable disconnect ONLY via connectionFault, never leadA/leadV.
Re-randomize hidden thresholds/signals within the Threshold Trainer bands.

mcqBank.note: Recognition + action stems per fault; options are built from faultActionMap (recognitionCorrect + distractors, correctActions + plausible wrong actions). Device-action decision points are auto-detected by the engine instead of MCQ.
mcqBank.recognitionStem: Look at the monitor and the device. What is happening?
wrongActionPool: Turn sensitivity all the way down (least sensitive)
Disconnect the wires to check the underlying rhythm
Silence the alarm and continue monitoring
Switch to a faster paced rate

threshold.label: Correct procedure
threshold.passWhen: rate set appropriately before testing; correct channel; non-pacing for sensing, pacing for stimulation

threshold.label: Threshold identified
threshold.passWhen: identified value within tolerance of the hidden ground-truth

threshold.label: Safe margin set
threshold.passWhen: output = 2x threshold (double; local training standard, not 3x) OR sensitivity <= 1/2 signal (sensing)

threshold.label: Safety & recognition
threshold.passWhen: no dependent patient stranded; recognized/flagged a high or bad-wire threshold; sensitivity not left undersensing

troubleshoot.label: Correct execution on device
troubleshoot.passWhen: engine detected the correct device action (capture/sensing/async/circuit)

troubleshoot.label: Safety
troubleshoot.passWhen: recognized dependence, used a bridge, avoided harmful actions (e.g., competition)

passingRule.threshold: identification AND margin must pass, with no safety fail
passingRule.troubleshoot: recognition AND priority_action AND execution must pass, with no safety fail
passingRule.overallPercent: weighted sum of category scores (pass=1, partial=0.5, fail=0) x 100

recordShape.caseId: string (drill id, PACE key, or generated id)

attemptsLog.storageNote: Separate localStorage key, never shared with any sync/state key; try/catch safe; degrades to in-memory. Mirrors vasoactive skillTracking.ts.

sharedWorkbook.buildDecision: xlsx requires vendoring SheetJS (breaks strict no-deps; acceptable as an inlined helper per CLAUDE.md QR exception) OR append CSV rows (zero-dep). Pick one; JSON/CSV per-attempt + Teams plumbing are dep-free either way.
